findings: Adopted September-2026 English Economics pathway, CROHO 56401, totals 180 unique EC. First two years sixty each; thirty-credit first-semester exchange and Spring six philosophy plus two six-credit electives plus twelve thesis. The two three-credit first-year programming units and year-two Competence/Big Data units are counted once. GROW carries no credits. No EOR-specific ISL or 144-credit rule is imported.

First mobility option is approved exchange, independently of UCR fit. At least twenty-four of thirty credits must be business/economics; all are bachelor-level English subjects, nonoverlapping and approved, excluding language/skills. Host/package remain open within those restrictions. Other minors/internship options are mutually exclusive and not added. First two adopted elective menu entries, Competition Policy and Regulation and Environmental Economics, are selected neutrally; their twelve credits replace generic restricted space. Earlier microeconomics, mathematics, Python and Industrial Economics supply Competition preparation.

Economics thesis is source-informed independent research with question, literature-based hypothesis, method, findings and argument, written/presented in English. First-year skills and at least 120 EC from semester six, or 138 from semester seven, are explicit. The ordinary example completes first-year R/Python and 150 EC before Spring. Registration and timely approved proposal are necessary; a failed attempt needs a new topic with at least one semester between attempts. No unsupported word count or separate practical requirement is invented.

All fifty interests were reconciled: sixteen direct generators, twenty curricular support topics, seven examples and seven conditional outcomes. Closest owns eleven generators, public/institutional candidate three, finance one and separately evidenced behavioural experiments one at the maximum. The candidate concepts are coherent academic purposes, not residual generator buckets. Experimental economics remains available but is not compulsory in the selected Competition/Environment external route.

Closest strengthens actual quantitative economics with Python and linear algebra instead of product design/organisational psychology. Its economics/finance/econometrics spine is complemented by concrete consumer/firm and technological-change inquiry. Public/institutional economics connects policy models and econometrics to legal, political, social, governance and implementation evidence; law/society replaces inaccessible constitutional selection, and actual Public Policy Analysis replaces unrelated American-history research. Finance replaces digital strategy with numerical mathematical modelling and makes banking/market decisions and quantitative methods central. No unsupported optimisation or specialist-finance degree claim remains.

Forty-two selected course contributions were assessed from available actual content, giving description-only Econometrics, calculus, databases, Behavioral Economics, Strategy, Market Research and Public Policy Analysis full supported consideration. All three complete schedules pass covered offerings, earlier prerequisites, four courses per term, first-year PPD and advanced-credit rules. Six offering conflicts and a missing prerequisite are repaired; five substitutions have specific content purposes. Pairwise differences of 105, 30 and 105 credits each way change academic priorities as well as passing the numerical floor.

R data workflows genuinely relate to R Programming; econometrics shares regression/IV but uses Stata versus R; microeconomics is placed with imperfect-market/industrial theory rather than treating behavioural experiments as game theory. Environmental governance and environmental economics share policy questions with explicit governance versus valuation/resource-model differences. General ethics is not historical economic thought.
